column1: # Maps each tests/test_*.sh suite to the paths it exercises, so
# .github/workflows/shell-tests.yml can select only the tests relevant to a
# PR's changed files. Built by reading each test's header comment and the
# guessed) — see the PR description for the audit.
#   test    - path to the test file, relative to repo root
#   globs   - semicolon-separated list of path globs this test exercises
#             (always includes the test's own path). A changed file matching
#             ANY of these globs makes this test "relevant" for the PR.
#   status  - "run" (executed in CI) or "skip-ci" (never run in CI)
#   reason  - required when status=skip-ci; empty for status=run
# A PR that changes .github/workflows/shell-tests.yml or this map file runs
# ALL status=run tests, regardless of the glob match (see the workflow).
# Scope note: this map covers only the top-level tests/test_*.sh suites
# test_*.sh, and every tests/test_*.R / tests/testthat/** suite are out of
# scope for this PR (R suites are a follow-up; the two sh files under
# tests/hooks/ and tests/codex_fallback/ were not part of the requested
# glob and are not audited here).

column4: confirmed via two real CI runs (JohnGavin/llm#1279, both "23 passed, 1 failed"): the test's own precondition self-check asserts `gh` is NOT found under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, true on the author's Homebrew Mac but false on ubuntu-latest, which ships gh at /usr/bin/gh — not fixable via a CI shim without removing gh from the runner's own PATH
macOS-only: bin/launchd_health_audit.sh hardcodes PLUTIL=/usr/bin/plutil with no override; plutil does not exist on Linux runners

requires nix-shell: bin/launchd_health_weekly_cron.sh hardcodes NIX_SHELL_BIN=/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix-shell with no override, and exits 1 before Step 1/2 when that binary is absent — nix is not installed on ubuntu-latest CI runners (same class of gap as test_launchd_health_audit.sh/test_launchd_run_record_timeout.sh)

macOS-only: confirmed via a real CI run (JohnGavin/llm#1279) — bin/launchd_run_record.sh calls `/usr/bin/time -l` (a BSD/macOS-only flag for RSS reporting); GNU time on Linux rejects `-l` outright, so the wrapped command never runs and every assertion sees a blank ledger row

observed failing on the Linux CI runner (4 PASS, 6 FAIL — JohnGavin/llm#1279) while passing cleanly on macOS (10/10, verified locally); root cause not isolated within this PR's scope — tracked as a follow-up

pre-existing bug, not a Linux/macOS difference (reproduced locally on macOS, 10/12 PASS): the test's own sqlite fixture creates `reviews` without a `structured_output` column, but roborev_bridge_to_unified.sh's query references rv.structured_output unconditionally — schema drift, tracked as a follow-up

requires Rscript (R toolchain) on PATH — R-dependent tests are deferred to the R/testthat CI follow-up noted in this PR (see also test_roborev_severity_consistency.sh, which degrades gracefully instead of hard-failing when Rscript is absent)

macOS-only: confirmed via a real CI run (JohnGavin/llm#1279) — the script's own --selftest test 9b calls `date -r <epoch-seconds>` expecting BSD semantics (epoch to clock time); GNU date's `-r` means "use this file's mtime" instead, so the assertion always sees an empty result on Linux. ghostscript+tesseract-ocr install as a shim worked fine; this is unrelated to that

partly macOS-only, partly pre-existing (JohnGavin/llm#1279): 3 of 5 CI failures are lib_signal_process_guard.sh's _signal_daemon_stdout_log() hard-depending on `plutil` (no Linux equivalent, not overridable by this test); the other 2 (PDF wiring) reproduce identically on macOS (44/46 passed locally) and are unrelated to platform — both tracked as follow-ups

observed failing heavily on the Linux CI runner (16 PASS, 11 FAIL — JohnGavin/llm#1279) while passing cleanly on macOS (27/27, verified locally); root cause not isolated within this PR's scope — tracked as a follow-up
macOS-only: calls `plutil -lint` unconditionally with no availability check or fallback; plutil does not exist on Linux runners
